claims.text: Temperatures from 600°C to 1200°C activate local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Temperatures from 600°C to 1200°C activate or alter short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated lattice distortions and short-range-order variations mediate a decrease in yield strength.
Thermally activated lattice distortions and short-range-order variations mediate a decrease in elastic modulus.
Thermally activated lattice distortions and short-range-order variations increase the thermal expansion coefficient relative to baseline conditions.
The proposed specimens are as-cast, polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr produced by arc melting.
The as-cast specimens are macroscopically compositionally homogeneous but contain atomistic-scale variations.
Elevated temperature promotes atomic reconfiguration in HfNbTaTiZr.
The thermally promoted atomic reconfigurations enhance local strain fields.
The proposed microstructural changes reduce effective bond rigidity.
Reduced effective bond rigidity lowers the elastic modulus.
Reduced effective bond rigidity lowers the yield strength.
The alloy will show statistically significant reductions in yield strength and elastic modulus relative to the ambient or minimally evolved baseline.
The alloy will show an increased thermal expansion coefficient relative to the baseline.
Changes in yield strength, elastic modulus, and thermal expansion will correlate with increased lattice microstrain.
Changes in yield strength, elastic modulus, and thermal expansion will correlate with diffraction-detectable shifts in short-range order.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate under controlled mechanical loading between 600°C and 1200°C.
Outside 600°C to 1200°C, activation of the proposed microstructural mechanisms may not be significant.
